long_biography.plain_text:
Alexander Nesis trained in radiochemistry at the Leningrad Technological Institute and worked at the Baltic Shipyard. During the late Soviet period, he found a commercial use for waste from uranium production in Uzbekistan. Producing rare-earth materials generated the capital that helped launch ICT Group in the early 1990s.

Nesis developed ICT as an industrial project builder rather than a permanent operator. The group bought and restructured shipbuilding, banking, rail-engineering and mining assets, and created Polymetal in 1998 around gold and silver deposits. Its strategy was to establish projects, add engineering and management capability, then sell once they could stand independently. The later ICT Holding continued that investment model after the original Russian group was reorganised.
long_biography.html:
Alexander Nesis trained in radiochemistry at the Leningrad Technological Institute and worked at the Baltic Shipyard. During the late Soviet period, he found a commercial use for waste from uranium production in Uzbekistan. Producing rare-earth materials generated the capital that helped launch ICT Group in the early 1990s.

Nesis developed ICT as an industrial project builder rather than a permanent operator. The group bought and restructured shipbuilding, banking, rail-engineering and mining assets, and created Polymetal in 1998 around gold and silver deposits. Its strategy was to establish projects, add engineering and management capability, then sell once they could stand independently. The later ICT Holding continued that investment model after the original Russian group was reorganised.
